tier_reason: The README Benchmarks section times r32x16b_avx2, rANS_static4x16, rANS_static4c (the CRAM rANS codec) and arith_static on an i5-4570 with gcc 6.2.0, clang 3.7.0 and icc 15.0.0, and every quoted number matches. The harness (TEST_MAIN in each .c) is public, but the Q8/Q40 inputs are not shipped and the README does not tie the Makefile flags to these runs, so the first-party numbers are not reproducible enough for A; C stands.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 92 stars, 6 forks; README points to samtools/htscodecs as the maintained successor
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers only. The Q8/Q40 test files are not shipped in the repo, so the run cannot be reproduced exactly (sample lines are shown in the README). The baselines are the author's own earlier rANS and arithmetic coder variants (rANS_static4c is the CRAM codec), not Huffman, FSE or ryg_rans itself. Order-1 results are not like-for-like: the README says the 4x16 family uses 9-bit order-1 frequency tables against 12 bits in 4x8/4c, and r32x16b_avx2 compresses order-1 slightly worse (15,872,840 vs 15,849,499 bytes on Q8). The r32x16b_avx2 order-1 encoder is not SIMD (TODO in the source). The third icc block is labelled 'order 0' but appears to be the order-1 run (README typo). The Makefile flags (-O3 -g -mtune=native, plus -march=core-avx2 for the AVX2 builds) are the current ones; the README does not state which flags produced the tables. Compilers are old (gcc 6.2, clang 3.7, icc 15) and the test CPU is a 2013 Haswell. There is no licence file, and the GitHub sidebar shows none. Embedded ryg_rans code is public domain, but the repo itself states no licence, so treat it as reference only. The maintained, more heavily SIMD-optimised successor htscodecs is already catalogued. Compiled AVX-512 variants exist in the source but are commented out of the Makefile and absent from the README results.

notes: Every number in claimed_speedup matches the README tables (derived ratios correctly labelled). License null and usability reference confirmed (no LICENSE/COPYING file; sidebar shows none). Last commit 2022-03-15 (a README update; the last code commit was 2018-04-09) confirmed, which makes it abandoned. Not a fork.
